Fact: design_rationale
What to find: How and why key design choices in training were made.
Card sections that often contain it: Training, Design

Answer with status, value, quotes and section.

answer.value: The card explains its training choices. WiSE-FT interpolation toward the base uses λ = 0.25, so only a quarter of the fine-tuned delta is kept. λ was chosen by constrained optimisation: maximise in-domain score subject to minimal degradation on held-out benchmarks. The card says this conservative λ is the direct reason held-out capability survives. Checkpoint fusion averages intermediate SFT checkpoints selected by a diversity probe, instead of taking the final checkpoint. MGPO (entropy-weighted GRPO) uses a programmatic verifier with partial credit for loose matches and token-F1, so that all-fail prompt groups still produce gradient. A sibling arm without the conservative interpolation scored higher in-domain but lost roughly twelve points of held-out capability, so this release is the balanced point of that trade.
quotes:
**Checkpoint fusion** — parameter-space averaging of intermediate SFT checkpoints selected
   by a diversity probe, rather than taking the final checkpoint.

**WiSE-FT interpolation** toward the pretrained base, `W = (1 − λ)·W_base + λ·W_finetuned`
   with **λ = 0.25** — i.e. only a quarter of the fine-tuned delta is retained. λ was chosen by
   constrained optimisation: maximise in-domain score subject to minimal degradation on held-out
   benchmarks. This conservative λ is the direct reason held-out capability survives.

**MGPO** — entropy-weighted GRPO reinforcement learning against a programmatic verifier, with
   partial credit for loose matches and token-F1 so that all-fail prompt groups still produce
   gradient.

A sibling arm that skipped stage 3's conservative interpolation scores considerably higher
in-domain (macro gate 0.515) but gives back roughly twelve points of held-out capability. This
release is the balanced point of that trade; the other was not published.
